column3: A palace-fortress rising from a red hill above Lhasa, once the winter home of the Dalai Lamas. Its white and red walls and golden roofs make it the symbol of Tibet. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The most sacred temple in Tibet, built in the seventh century in the old city of Lhasa. Pilgrims prostrate in front of its doors, and inside it holds a revered statue of the Buddha.
A circuit around the Jokhang Temple, full of pilgrims spinning prayer wheels, and stalls selling prayer flags, jewelry and butter lamps.
A summer palace and garden of the Dalai Lamas, with pavilions, trees and ponds, where Tibetans picnic in summer.
Once one of the largest monasteries in the world, with white buildings that climb a hillside, and housing thousands of monks.
A monastery famed for its monks' debates in the courtyard, where they clap and argue about Buddhist teachings in the afternoon.
A great salt lake high on the plateau, at about 4,700 meters, with a deep turquoise color under a vast sky and with snow peaks beyond. It is one of Tibet's sacred lakes.
A museum of Tibetan history and art, with thangka paintings, religious objects and displays on daily life on the plateau.
Tea churned with yak butter and salt, a hot, rich drink that warms Tibetans at high altitude, and which welcomes every guest.
Roasted barley flour, the staple of Tibet. You mix it with butter tea and knead it into a ball with your fingers.
Thick noodles in a beef broth, a warm, simple meal in Lhasa's noodle shops.
Dried or stewed yak, with a rich flavor and lean meat, a staple of the plateau.
Chang is a mild drink made from barley, offered at festivals and weddings, often accompanied by song.
A thick, sweet yogurt from yak milk, a Tibetan favorite, especially at the Shoton Festival.
Momo are dumplings filled with yak or beef, steamed or fried, eaten with a hot chili sauce.
A sweet milky tea, sold in Lhasa's teahouses, where people gather to talk over cheap, hot glasses of tea.
Losar is the Tibetan New Year, with family feasts, prayers, new clothes and offerings of barley and fried cakes.
A summer festival in Lhasa, with a giant thangka painting unveiled on a hillside, plus Tibetan opera and yogurt feasts.
Tibetan opera is a masked drama that combines song, dance and storytelling, often about Buddhist tales.
Thangka are painted scrolls of Buddhist figures, made with mineral pigments and gold, and take months or years to complete.
The seat of the Panchen Lamas in Shigatse, with a giant gilded statue of Maitreya, the Buddha of the future.
A fortress-like monastery painted in red, white and gray, the center of the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism.
The highest mountain in the world, at 8,849 meters, on the border of Tibet and Nepal. Its Tibetan name is Chomolungma.
The Tibetan base camp on the north side of Everest, with a tent village and a view of the north face.
A monastery in Gyantse with a nine-story stupa that holds thousands of paintings and statues.
A fortress on a hill above Gyantse, which saw a battle in 1904 and has a wide view over the town.
A turquoise lake shaped like a scorpion, one of the three great sacred lakes of Tibet, with mountain views.
A glacier by the roadside where you can see the ice from a view platform, at a high mountain pass.
A small, black pig of the plateau, raised in the mountains and known for its tender and tasty meat.
Bread fried in butter, crisp outside and soft inside, a popular snack at festivals.
A thick yogurt from the milk of yaks, tangy and creamy, sold in many homes in the villages.
The deepest canyon in the world, which the Yarlung Tsangpo River cuts around the eastern end of the Himalayas, in a steep, green gorge.
A snow peak at the bend of the river, often hidden by clouds, so that seeing it is considered a gift.
A forest lake in a valley of pines and snow peaks, with a temple on a small island and calm, clear water.
A pass with views of Namcha Barwa on a clear day, among rhododendron forests.
A forest and meadow that look like an alpine landscape, with wooden houses and grazing cattle.
Wild matsutake mushrooms from the forests of Nyingchi, prized for their aroma, and served in soup or grilled.
Chicken cooked with herbs in a stone pot from Mêdog, where the soapstone gives the soup its special taste.
A small people of the forests near the Himalayas, known for their wooden bowls and bamboo crafts.
A small people in the far southeast of Tibet, known for their hunting traditions and bamboo and cane crafts.
An ancient palace on a hill that is said to have been built in the second century BCE as the first palace of Tibet.
The first Buddhist monastery in Tibet, built in the eighth century in the shape of a mandala, with halls and stupas around a central temple.
Burial mounds of the Tibetan emperors of the seventh to ninth centuries, grassy hills in a valley with stone pillars.
A flatbread made of barley flour, baked or toasted, a traditional food of the farming valleys.
Tibetan medicine is a medical system with centuries of history, which uses herbs, minerals, diet and massage.
Dried yak meat is chewy and savory, an ideal snack for long journeys across the plateau.
A holy mountain for Buddhists, Hindus, Jains and Bon followers, shaped like a four-sided pyramid. No one is allowed to climb it, but pilgrims walk around it.
A holy lake near Mount Kailash, among the highest freshwater lakes in the world, where pilgrims bathe for blessing.
Lamb from the high plateau of Ngari, with a tender, sweet taste, grown on mountain grass.
The kora is a walk around the mountain, a circuit of about 52 kilometers, said to bring merit, which pilgrims complete in about three days.
